title: Act Apprentice (under the Apprenticeship Act, 1961)
qualification: Candidates must have passed the 10th class examination or its equivalent (under the 10+2 system) with a minimum of 50% aggregate marks from a recognised board, and must also possess a National Trade Certificate (NTC) in the notified trade issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT).
salary: As per extant rules & directives issued by Railway Board from time to time. || No Hostel accommodation will be provided and selected candidates will have to make their own arrangement during their training as per Apprentices Act. 1961 and they will be released on completion of the training.
age_limit: Candidates should have completed 15 years of age and should not have completed 24 years of age as on 05.09.2026. || Candidates claiming reservation benefits must produce the relevant caste, non-creamy layer, disability, or discharge certificate, as applicable, issued by the appropriate authority at the time of document verification. || To avoid any confusion regarding age eligibility, candidates can use our Age Calculator to calculate their exact age based on the prescribed cut-off date before applying.
application_fee: The fee is payable only through the online payment gateway (debit card, credit card, internet banking, SBI challan, etc.) integrated with the application form; cash, cheque, money order, or demand draft are not accepted. Payment must be completed within 2 working days of successfully filling the application, and no edits are allowed once the fee is paid. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other examination.
selection_process: Selection is based on a merit list, without any written examination or interview, prepared as follows: || The merit list is based on the simple average of the percentage of marks in matriculation (minimum 50% aggregate) and the percentage of marks in the ITI/NTC certificate for the relevant trade. || Matriculation percentage is calculated using marks obtained in all subjects, not just a selected group of subjects. || In case of a tie in marks, the older candidate is preferred; if the date of birth is also the same, the candidate who passed matriculation earlier is preferred. || A final merit list is prepared trade-wise and community-wise, in descending order of marks, equal to the number of available seats. || Shortlisted candidates are called for Document Verification, where original certificates and a medical fitness certificate are checked. Call letters for document verification may be issued to up to 1.5 times the number of identified slots. || Selected candidates must also be found medically fit as per the standards prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961 and the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992.

title: Physical Training Instructor (PTI), Primary Cadre
qualification: As per Appendix 'B' of the Punjab State Elementary Education (Physical Training Instructor) Service Rules, 2023 (as amended in 2025), candidates must have passed 10+2 along with at least a two-year diploma or certificate in Physical Education , referred to as Diploma in Physical Education or Certificate in Physical Education (D.P.Ed/C.P.Ed) or an equivalent course under any other nomenclature. || Candidates who are in the final year of their D.P.Ed/C.P.Ed diploma or certificate course are also eligible to apply, provided they successfully complete and pass the diploma/certificate before the final recruitment merit list date (the deadline for this is the final recruitment merit list date, not the last date of this recruitment process). || Additionally, as per Punjab Government notification G.S.R.72/Const./Art.309/Amd.(22)/2022 dated 28-10-2022, candidates must have passed Matriculation with Punjabi as a compulsory or elective subject , or an equivalent examination in Punjabi. Candidates who have not studied Punjabi at the Matric level must clear a qualifying Punjabi language test with a minimum of 50% marks; failing this will disqualify the candidate from the final merit list irrespective of their score in the main written test.
salary: Selected candidates will be engaged on a fixed pay scale as per the Punjab State Elementary Education (Physical Training Instructor) Service Rules, 2023, and its First Amendment Rules, 2025.
age_limit: Upper age limit relaxed by their length of service, minus 3 years, subject to prescribed conditions
application_fee: Fee relaxation for ex-servicemen is applicable only if the candidate's post-retirement employment with the Central Government or its undertakings has been completed, or the candidate was not discharged from service on disciplinary grounds. Ex-servicemen and their dependents must submit the applicable relaxation certificate, including a Lineal Descendent Certificate (LDC) for dependents, at the time of document verification. No fee refund will be given, even in case of a wrong claim of category-based fee concession, and candidates found to have made an incorrect claim will be blacklisted from all recruitments conducted by the Director, Education Recruitment Directorate, Punjab for three years.
selection_process: Selection for the PTI (Primary Cadre) posts will be based on a combined merit prepared from a written test and sports achievement weightage, as per the following distribution out of a total of 100 marks. || The written test will be a single objective multiple-choice paper of 70 marks conducted at the state level. Candidates must also clear the Physical Eligibility Test (PET), which is qualifying in nature and does not carry marks in the merit calculation. || Sports achievement weightage does not apply to candidates recruited under the sports quota; for these candidates, the Punjab Sportsmen Recruitment Rules, 1988, remain applicable. In case of multiple gradation certificates, a candidate can claim weightage for only one gradation certificate issued as per the revised Gradation Policy, 2023, of the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Punjab. || As per Punjab Government notification dated 28-10-2022, candidates must also clear a qualifying Punjabi language paper with a minimum of 50% marks at the Matriculation standard, in addition to the competitive written test. If two or more candidates score the same marks in the written test, the older candidate will be given preference in merit; if age is also the same, the candidate with a higher percentage of marks in their professional/educational qualification will be preferred.
